profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap way in Nebraska is tagged telecom=data_center under the name Compute North, matching a real company by that name that operated as a Bitcoin mining hosting business headquartered in Minnesota. Compute North built and ran large-scale cryptocurrency mining sites in multiple US states, hosting mining hardware for institutional clients rather than operating a conventional colocation or cloud data center business. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September 2022, one of several mining hosting firms to do so as falling cryptocurrency prices and rising energy costs squeezed the industry that year, and its facilities and contracts were subsequently sold off or restructured through the bankruptcy process. Because this entry could not be independently re-verified this session (WebSearch quota was exhausted, and Compute North's own former web presence has reportedly gone dark since the bankruptcy), the current operational status of this specific Nebraska site, whether it continued mining under a successor owner, was idled, or was decommissioned, is not confirmed here. This record should be read as identifying a genuine former cryptocurrency mining hosting operation rather than a conventional data center, with its post-2022 status flagged as an open question for future research rather than assumed either way.
profile.research_note: Compute North was a real, named Bitcoin mining hosting company headquartered in Minnesota that operated large-scale mining sites in several states including Nebraska, Texas, and South Dakota. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September 2022 amid the broader crypto-mining industry downturn, and its assets were subsequently sold or wound down through the bankruptcy process (its Texas and other US sites were acquired by other operators including Generate Capital-backed buyers). This OSM way in Nebraska carries the Compute North name; given the company's 2022 bankruptcy, the facility's current operating status (still mining under a successor owner, idle, or decommissioned) could not be confirmed this session due to search-tool quota limits, so this entry documents the company's known history and flags the site's present status as unconfirmed rather than asserting it is still active.

reading.body:
This campus in Buffalo County published 30 megawatts of IT capacity as of July 2022. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common density for AI training, 30 megawatts of IT load converts to roughly 750 racks. An announced expansion to 100 megawatts was never confirmed as built.

Compute North filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2022, one month after this facility was reported operating. Local news reported the site continued operating after the filing, but current post-bankruptcy ownership is not independently confirmed as of this reading. The operator name on file remains Compute North pending a follow-up verification.

Nebraska has 21 mapped data center facilities on record. This campus is the only one in the state with a published megawatt figure, making it rank first by disclosed capacity. No other facility in Nebraska has released specifications to this site, so the state's actual operating capacity is unknown and likely substantially larger than the single confirmed figure here.
